content.comment_body: Hello, Here’s a quick summary of my [product_name] program: Start → 30 second delay → switch on green light. The delay works fine, but I'd like to add a PAUSE button. Specifically, when pressing PAUSE, the countdown stops, and it resumes when this input is released. Is it possible to achieve this with [product_name]? Thanks!
Hi! Try this approach. Hope it helps!

Hi, Here’s more context related to [user_name]'s solution: The approach is correct since [product_name] does not have a timing block that can be paused using an external signal. The only option is to create a custom timer using a pulse generator and counter(s), similar to [user_name]'s suggestion. To minimize timing errors (especially if the pause signal frequency is high), set TH = TL and keep TH + TL small. You’ll also need a sufficiently high [product_name] cycle frequency. In some cases, it may help to add a pre-divider between the pulse generator and main counter (constructed with a counter and a marker at the counter output, and a signal line to the CLR pin of this counter—ON = OFF sets the pre-divider value). With this, you can achieve a time base of 0.05 s + 0.05 s = 0.1 s and use a secondary counter for full seconds. See also similar questions: "Can I pause timers or programs". Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are trying to add pause functionality to a countdown timer controlled via [product_name]. They note that built-in timing features do not allow pausing with an external signal, leading to discussions about custom workarounds using pulse generators and counters. This reveals a gap between users’ expectations of straightforward timer control and the actual options provided by the [product_name] platform.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to pause and resume a countdown timer with a simple configuration using an external input, such as a pause button, in [product_name] devices.
